title: Compatibility gates for structured-output and function-call behavior during rollouts
creator: Priya Menon
description:
Problem: As we expand function-calling and structured-output use in customer workloads, naive canary/A/B rollouts miss incompatibilities: schema shape changes, missing required fields, and divergent function-call argument shapes can silently break downstream consumers. Goal: add automated compatibility gates to rollout pipelines that detect and block/regress model variants which change structured outputs or function-call behavior beyond configurable thresholds.

Scope and deliverables:
1) Schema conformance check (runtime): ingest a configurable percentage of canary and shadow traffic and validate outputs against the expected JSON schema (including required fields, field types, enum constraints). Produce per-request pass/fail and aggregate pass rate.
2) Function-call diffs: capture function-call invocations (name + args) from baseline and candidate models and compute diffs: missing calls, new calls, arg-type mismatches, and argument value divergence for critical keys. Provide a summarized diff score and top-k example mismatches.
3) Canary gate policy: extend rollout policy language to include schema_pass_rate and function_call_compat_score thresholds. Gates evaluate after a configurable sample window (min requests and min time). If thresholds fail, trigger auto-rollback or canary extension according to policy.
4) Shadow traffic capture: wire shadow mode to duplicate traffic to candidate without impacting production. Store a sampled set of requests/responses for offline analysis. Ensure PII handling and retention controls.
5) Console UX: add gate status, top schema errors, and representative function-call diffs to the rollout dashboard and Slack/PagerDuty alerts.
6) Performance budget: aim for <5% added p99 latency and <8% CPU/GPU overhead for shadow capture at default sampling.
7) Tests and QA: synthetic tests with crafted schema-breaking variants, integration tests for gating logic, and staged rollout to internal teams.

Design notes and trade-offs:
- We will do lightweight validation at the edge (schema structure) and more expensive diffs in an async job to avoid blocking inference. Edge checks will be schema-pass/fail; diff aggregation will run with eventual consistency and will inform gate evaluation only after enrichment completes.
- To avoid false positives due to natural output variance, function-call diffs will use a weighted scoring model: missing required calls are high-severity, new optional calls low-severity, and arg-type mismatches medium. Admins can map functions/fields to severity buckets per project.
- Shadow capture will be sampled and stored encrypted. Full request/response recording is opt-in per workspace with explicit retention configuration to meet compliance needs.
- Backwards compatibility: rollout gate defaults will be conservative (e.g., schema_pass_rate >= 99.5%, function_call_compat_score >= 98%) and opt-in for older clients that accept looser contracts.

Acceptance criteria (pass/fail):
- The runtime emits per-request schema validation events and aggregated pass rates for canary and shadow traffic.
- The rollout policy language accepts schema_pass_rate and function_call_compat_score thresholds and enforces them during canaries.
- Console shows gate evaluation timeline, top schema errors, and representative function-call diffs for failing canaries.
- Auto-rollback triggers when configured thresholds are breached and records a rollout event (with reason) in the audit log.
- End-to-end tests demonstrating a model with a missing required field gets stopped by the gate and does not reach 100% traffic.

Implementation plan (high level):
- Week 1: schema validation library integration (jsonschema + custom type checks), event schema for validation results, and instrumentation for canary path.
- Week 2: function-call capture hook, diff proto design, and offline aggregator service prototype.
- Week 3: rollout policy extension, gate evaluator, and unit tests.
- Week 4: Console integration, dashboards, alerts, and internal dogfood.

Links and artifacts:
- Design doc: https://docs.google.com/document/d/1a2b-rollout-structured-output
- GH prototype PR (schema validation): https://github.com/redwood-inference/rollouts/pull/1298
- Dogfood checklist: https://drive.redwood.ai/rollouts/dogfood-checklist

Notes on privacy/security: recordings will be encrypted at rest with KMS and access-controlled. We will add a data-minimization mode that strips payloads to the minimal fields needed for compatibility checks. Security review required before enabling workspace-level recording.

Longer-term ideas (out of scope for this ticket): semantic argument equivalence detection, automated migration hints (mapping rules that transform older clients), and contract versioning tied to model metadata.
